Experimental status

Prepared does not mean executed.

Neither track has QPU data in the supplied evidence. No experimental acceptance rule or independent preregistration is asserted by this release.

Track A · trapped-ion conformance

PREPARED DRAFT · NOT EXECUTED

A nine-qubit logical test of the X-only repetition controller. It does not demonstrate native tetrahedral hardware or a protected memory under general Pauli noise.

A bounded first review

The release includes a version-frozen 20-circuit draft inventory: 16 clean X-pattern syndrome checks and four baseline/control templates. The logical Stim files are parseable and their ideal expectations are checked. They are not vendor-compiled pulse schedules.

Start with the 16 patterns and a paired coherence/crosstalk control review. The historical 1,450-variant inventory is not the first execution request. Single-round syndrome circuits do not themselves implement the full adaptive controller.

Before an experimental freeze

  • A named collaborator, mapping, interaction schedule and compiled circuits.
  • Calibrated gate, idle, measurement/reset and crosstalk behavior.
  • Matched control durations, shot counts, loss handling and decoder latency.
  • Predeclared acceptance and rejection rules, then non-constructor review.

These remain open. No QPU work has been submitted.

Track B · native 3D geometry

GEOMETRY PROPOSAL · NOT EXECUTED

A tetrahedral-plus-center placement and ancilla motion proposal. No apparatus, calibrated fidelity model, or demonstrated state-sensitive 0/1/loss readout is supplied. It is not an offered work package.

The proposed partner-switch path λR is a geometric length: R is the center-to-vertex radius and λ the approach fraction. It is not a gate time or fidelity. A physical specification still needs site separations, drive parameters, crosstalk dynamics, timing and readout/control constraints.

Gates in a native 3D register with ancillas moved to a readout zone must be reported separately from static multilayer readout. No such device capability is claimed here.

Benjamin Walker Mayes
